result:
task: Correct the W2-95 acceptance tests so they find `gov check`'s checks and families in both its success form (`result`) and its failure form (`error.details`), with no expectation changed.
status: DONE. The correction is committed. Against `w2/integrate`'s code the run gives the README's counts and reasons.
work_completed: Step 0 sandbox check first. (a) Writing `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-DAEO-57hm` failed with `OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`, as required. (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` printed a hash, and `git update-index --refresh` exited 0. Identity: `GOV_ROLE=independent-test-designer`, `GOV_TICKET=DAEO-57hm`, top level `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-95-tests`, branch `w2/W2-95-tests`. I confirmed the failure form in `src/gov/check/command.py`, which raises `GovError("CHECK_FAILED", …, details=result, exit_code=3)`, and in `src/gov/cli/main.py:180-182`, which builds the envelope with `error.details`. Both files are the same on `w2/integrate`. In `w2_95_support.py`, `GovCheck` gained `failed_form()` and `answered()`, and `result` now returns `error.details` when the code is `CHECK_FAILED` and `result` otherwise. Any other answer (no JSON, or another error code) is still a refusal. In `_gov_pathmap`, the condition `ok is True` became `answered()`; this fixes the three cases named in the brief, and their names are unchanged. I made the same fix to a fourth case, `test_w2_95_missing_path_map_is_never_green_in_gov_check`. It treated every `ok: false` as a refusal, so it would have read a red core-pathmap's failure form as a refusal and checked only that the error text names `path-map.yaml`. It now reads that form as the check's answer and makes its full assertions: not green, has findings, family not green. Its refusal branch still covers every other error. The README now describes both forms and has a "Revision (test batch 2)" section.

It touches 4 files (+46/−8). `git log --oneline -2` shows 1f2e219940fa, then ba0f1bd51a0a. After the commit, `git status --short` shows no tracked changes, only untracked dotfiles at the worktree root that were not mine (.bashrc, .gitconfig, .mcp.json, .idea, .vscode and similar) and that I did not touch. gov.__file__: `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-95-tests/src/gov/__init__.py`. A scratch script fed `GovCheck` the three answer forms. Failure form (CHECK_FAILED): answered True, core-pathmap RED, family RED. Success form: answered True, RED, RED. Another error code (CONFIG_INVALID): answered False, nothing read.
tests: `PYTHONPATH=/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-95-tests/src python3 -m pytest tests/acceptance/W2-95 -q -p no:cacheprovider -o tmp_path_retention_policy=failed` gave 22 failed, 6 passed out of 28, the same as the README states. The four `gov check` cases fail for the README's reasons. `gov_check_family_is_not_green_…` fails on `'GREEN' != 'GREEN'` ("a path in no namespace is reported green"). `missing_path_map_is_never_green_in_gov_check` fails on `'GREEN' != 'GREEN'` ("a missing path map is reported green"). `adopted_repository_names_each_…` fails first at the declared command ("…is green", exit 0). `other_checks_results_do_not_change_…` passes, as before. The other 18 failures and 5 passes are unchanged from the README.
discoveries: On `w2/integrate`, core-pathmap is never red through `gov check`: the mapping form is not judged, and a list-form path map is refused by the loader with CONFIG_INVALID. So the failure-form path cannot be reached by a real run on that code. I checked it against the exact envelope the CLI builds instead.
risks: The failure-form reading is checked against a hand-built envelope that follows `main.py:180-182`, not a live red run. It will first run live against the engineer's implementation.
lessons: Any test that reads `gov check --json` must read `error.details` whenever `error.code == "CHECK_FAILED"`. A red hard-block check never leaves its checks under `result`.
